/** *

Gets the locale used by this formatter.

ownership_reason: Only the gold interprets the field: it finds the level that holds it, sets every finer level to its minimum and moves that level one unit up. Hops 1-4 copy the date into a Calendar, refuse a year over 280 million, supply the table of levels and pass everything on, and their javadocs say the calendar and the field are handed on unchanged. The next unit of SEMI_MONTH is half a month (the SEMI_MONTH constant: 'This is half a month'; the facade: 'the field from Calendar or SEMI_MONTH'): days 1-15 move to the 16th, days 16-31 to the first of the next month. DateUtils.modify takes exactly that step for truncate, round and the Calendar overload of ceiling, and DateUtilsRoundingTest testTruncateSemiMonth / testRoundSemiMonth and DateUtilsTest testTruncate / testRound pin it and pass. Once the gold has moved the day one unit the half-month result is lost to every caller, and no one-line change of the table helps: SEMI_MONTH on the day level moves one day, on the month level (as in DateUtils.fields) one month, in no row it is refused.
